title: The questions, and what each one teaches
dek: Every worked question on the site, the core challenge it trains, and an order to take them in.

body.x: Every worked question follows the six steps in 'How to answer a system design question': requirements, the numbers that matter, entities and API, a high-level design, deep dives, and what's expected at each level. In the workspace, the same question has example tests to run while you design, more tests that run when you submit, hints that cost points, and the worked answer as its solution.

head: Question
What it trains
rows: Design a URL shortener
Unique short codes and redirects at lakhs a second
Design file storage and sync
Big files on patchy networks, devices kept in step
Design restaurants near me
Finding what is near a point, thousands of times a second
Design 10-minute grocery delivery
Never selling the last packet twice, inside a time budget
Design photo sharing
Images served fast, and a like count for a viral dish
Design a notification service
An OTP never stuck behind a promotion, never sent twice
Design a live leaderboard
Keeping lakhs of players sorted, and your own rank cheaply
body.label: Easy questions

head: Question
What it trains
rows: Design a news feed
Push or pull, and the follower with 50 lakh followers
Design dating app swipes
Recording every swipe and spotting each match exactly once
Design a coding judge
Running strangers' code safely, and the last-15-minutes rush
Design a chat app
Messages to the phone in order, with nothing lost
Design a job scheduler
Finding what is due, and surviving 9 pm
Design video streaming
Getting videos ready fast and playing them smoothly
Design menu search
Words, Hinglish, typos and ranking
body.label: Medium questions

head: Question
What it trains
rows: Design match ticket booking
A crowd 50 times larger than the seats, and no seat sold twice
Design a payment system
Charging exactly once, and "unknown" is not "failed"
Design a web crawler
Being polite, never fetching twice, avoiding traps
Design ad click counting
Fast enough to watch, exact enough to bill
Design a distributed key-value store
Where a key lives, and copies that agree enough
Design a shared document editor
Two people editing one line, and your typing feeling instant
Design rider assignment for food delivery
Live locations, and one order per rider
Design live streaming for IND vs PAK
3.5 crore people at once, and a crowd that arrives with the toss
body.label: Hard questions

body.x: An order to take them in

items: Week 1: the seven easy questions, in the order listed. They teach the method with one main problem each.
Week 2: the news feed, the chat app and the job scheduler: scaling reads, real-time updates and long jobs.
Week 3: match ticket booking, the payment system and ad click counting: contention, processes with many steps and scaling writes.
Then the rest, in any order. Redo your weakest question a week later.
